subject: MSA Addendum: customer quote cadence & brand usage controls
messages:
From: Jill Harper <jill.harper@neptuneanalytics.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: tom.riley@neptuneanalytics.com
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA addendum redline and publicity/logo language

Marissa,

Thanks for taking this — attaching our redlined version of the MSA addendum (Neptune_MSA_Redline_20271004.docx). Two quick asks from legal/marketing on our side that we highlighted in the doc: 

1) Publicity window: We need a 30-day post-launch publicity window where Neptune has the right to approve any press release or joint announcement that uses our logos or quotes.

2) Quotes & attribution: Any customer quote or case study using Neptune's name must be pre-approved in writing. If Redwood wants to use an anonymized excerpt (no company name), approval turnaround can be faster.

3) Logo usage: Logo usage limited to two placements (web + datasheet) unless we agree in writing. We added a carve-out for compliance-required mentions.

4) Opt-out: Neptune requests a unilateral right to opt out of being used as a customer reference for any reason; we'd be open to a limited cadence (e.g., one opt-out per year).

We highlighted specific language we think is non-starter for us in the doc and suggested alternatives inline. Can your team propose final language we can feed to our counsel?

Attachments: Neptune_MSA_Redline_20271004.docx

Best,

Jill Harper
Sr. Legal Counsel, Neptune Analytics

Hi Jill — thanks for the redline and the clear summary. Looping in Lauren (legal) and Kim (brand) to finalize language. Quick read and a couple of pragmatic options from our side so we can move to counsel: 

Option A (standard):
- Publicity window: Redwood requests a 45-day coordination window post-public launch to allow for joint messaging and customer success quotes.
- Approval: Written approval required for any quote that includes Neptune's name; Redwood will provide the first-draft quote and allow up to 10 business days for review.
- Logo: Two placements allowed (web + solution page). Additional placements require mutual written consent.

Option B (compromise):
- Publicity window: 30-day coordination window as requested by Neptune but with a mandatory pre-approved template for quotes and one consolidated logo asset package.
- Approval: If Neptune does not respond within 10 business days, silence will be treated as approval for the specific quote draft and logo usage.

We attached a short proposed clause (Proposed_Clause_Draft_20271004.txt) that maps to Option B (easier operationally). If Neptune prefers Option A, we can route for an exception and flag pricing/credits if their opt-out language remains unilateral.

Next steps: can you confirm which option you prefer and whether your counsel requires different approval timelines? Also, Jill — if you can provide an example of a 'single opt-out per year' scenario that Neptune expects, that helps legal write precise language.

Thanks — Marissa
Director, Customer Marketing (Redwood Inference)
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Marissa / Kim — forwarding Jill's original with inline suggestions below. I drafted two short clause variants to give Neptune: a conservative legal-first variant and an operational variant for sales to accept.

--- Forwarded message ---
From: Jill Harper <jill.harper@neptuneanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, Oct 4, 2027 at 09:12 AM
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Subject: MSA addendum redline and publicity/logo language

> 1) Publicity window: We need a 30-day post-launch publicity window...

Lauren (inline): Redwood prefers to retain the ability to coordinate joint messaging up to 45 days; however, we can accept 30 days if Neptune agrees to a 10-business-day approval SLA for quote/logo approvals.

> 2) Quotes & attribution: Any customer quote or case study using Neptune's name must be pre-approved in writing.

Lauren (inline): Suggest this be split: (a) Named quotes require explicit written approval; (b) anonymized excerpts (no identifiable reference) require acknowledgement but can be auto-approved after 5 business days. This keeps sales velocity while protecting Neptune.

> 3) Logo usage: Logo usage limited to two placements (web + datasheet) unless we agree in writing.

Lauren (inline): Propose limiting to two placements in commercial materials but allow exception for co-branded events and partner marketplace listings — subject to mutual written consent. Add a short definition of "placement" to avoid interpretation issues.

> 4) Opt-out: Neptune requests a unilateral right to opt out...

Lauren (inline): We cannot accept an unlimited unilateral opt-out. Propose: Neptune may request an opt-out once per 12-month period with 30 days' notice; additional opt-outs require mutual agreement or nominal consideration (credits or deferred public mention).

Attached: two clause drafts (legal_variant & ops_variant) — please review and tell me which we send to Jill. If we push the approval SLA to 10 business days we should be able to close without pricing impact.

— Lauren
General Counsel (acting), Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

From: Jill Harper <jill.harper@neptuneanalytics.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 6 Oct 2027 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA addendum redline and publicity/logo language

Hi all — thanks for the quick turn. We discussed Option B plus Lauren's inline points with our counsel and marketing. We can accept Option B with two adjustments: 

1) Approval SLA: 10 business days for named quotes and logo use is fine, but Neptune requires a 10 business day guaranteed turnaround (not silence-as-approval). If Redwood needs an auto-approve path for anonymized excerpts, 5 business days is acceptable.

2) Opt-out: Neptune will accept the limitation to one opt-out per 12-month period but requests that the opt-out be exercisable without penalty if the reason is regulatory compliance or a matter that could cause reputational risk.

If you can send the final clause language reflecting those two edits, I will run it with our legal team and sign off quickly.

We prefer to use DocuSign for the final addendum — here's our envelope (https://app.docusign.com/NEP-2027-0147).
